items.title: Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
items.detailText:
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 801,351,354 shares are being offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders. Anthropic also expects to grant the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of its Class A common stock.
The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”
The proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014.

items.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
items.detailText:
Today, we’re excited to introduce Muse Spark 1.1, the latest model from Meta Superintelligence Labs and a significant upgrade from Muse Spark. Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.
With these improvements, Muse Spark 1.1 advances the performance-efficiency frontier. Together with this week’s launch of Muse Image , this release brings us closer to our vision of personal superintelligence: models that help you pursue your goals, create what you imagine, deepen your relationships, and take action on what you value most.
Along with this release, we are launching a public preview of the new Meta Model API where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1. The model is available now in "Thinking" mode in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai .
For more details about our evaluations, see our report .
Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services. It zero-shot generalizes to new native tools, MCP servers, and custom skills.
It tackles complex projects significantly faster than Muse Spark, as it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency. As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents. As a subagent, it adheres to its job, understands available tools, and knows when to escalate back to the main agent.
Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens. It remembers actions, retrieves information from much earlier work, and compacts in a way that keeps the critical steps needed for later work.
Muse Spark 1.1 excels at computer-use workflows that unfold across multiple applications with information changing on-the-fly. It maintains context across extended sessions, adapts to evolving requirements, and navigates unfamiliar interfaces with minimal human intervention.
Rather than reasoning through every desktop step one click at a time, Muse Spark 1.1 understands when to automate and when to use the interface directly. We trained the model to write scripts when automation is faster, click when direct interaction is simpler, and generate batches of actions at each step.
Agentic dinner party organization: In real-world applications, new context arises that changes the task. Muse Spark 1.1 notices these changes when placing the dinner order and makes necessary updates without user intervention.

items.title: Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video
items.detailText:
Muse Image follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, composes from multiple references, and draws on Instagram for social context. Muse...
We’re excited to launch Muse Image and preview Muse Video, the first media generation models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Image is our most advanced image generation model yet: it follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, and composes from multiple references. It also brings agentic tool use capabilities and integrates with Muse Spark. Muse Video, built on the same pretraining base, delivers exceptional visual fidelity with native audio support.
Muse Image is available today across the Meta AI app and on meta.ai , Instagram Stories in the US, and WhatsApp in limited countries, and is coming soon to Facebook. Muse Video is coming soon to creators and Meta AI.
Instead of directly mapping prompts to images, Muse Image operates as an agent: it invokes search and coding tools to improve accuracy, self-refines its own generations, and improves through scaling test-time compute. Muse Image also integrates with Muse Spark, allowing the two models to share tools and plan jointly for powerful agentic media generation.
We provide Muse Image with access to tools to enhance its agentic capabilities.
Coding. During reinforcement learning, Muse Image learns to write and execute code that produces accurate plots and QR codes, and condition on rendered figures to improve the accuracy of generated images. Muse Spark and Muse Image also integrate to use the combination of code and media generation to create animated GIFs, websites with embedded images, and interactive visual games.
Search. Muse Image learns to search the web to ground generated images in factual and real-time information and visual references. Enabling search improves factual accuracy on knowledge-intensive prompts, particularly those involving current events and real-world facts.

items.description: The Three Hidden Bills of an LLM Proxy: Security Incidents, Operational Investment, and Model Selection This article introduces Alibaba Cloud AI Gateway, a secure, serverless LLM proxy that optimizes model routing and eliminates hidden oper
items.detailText:
This article introduces Alibaba Cloud AI Gateway, a secure, serverless LLM proxy that optimizes model routing and eliminates hidden operational costs.
Teams building large language model applications have probably gone through a similar evolution over the past year: first integrating a single model, then a whole group; setting up an LLM proxy to centrally manage API keys, metering, and rate limiting; and, as more and more models are added, encountering a new question—which model should handle each request?
Along this path, three bills rarely get calculated in advance: the cost of security incidents , the investment in building and maintaining the system yourself , and the model-selection logic scattered throughout application code . LiteLLM's experience in 2026 happens to offer an illustration of all three.
Vulnerabilities were similarly frequent: pre-authentication SQL injection (CVE-2026-42208, CVSS 9.8, exploited in the wild within 36 hours of the advisory's publication), command execution via an MCP test endpoint (CVE-2026-42271, already included in CISA KEV), MCP authentication bypass (CVE-2026-59822), and privilege escalation through virtual keys (CVE-2026-47101), among others. Several were rated CRITICAL.
Viewed individually, each incident can be attributed to "an account was stolen" or "a piece of code was poorly written." Taken together, however, they reveal a structural problem:
The first two are dictated by business requirements and cannot be avoided; the blast radius depends on the third. The key question is therefore not just "Will something go wrong?" but what malicious code can actually take away once it does.

items.title: 推理算力占比破七成，算力需求的重心正从峰值转向长尾
items.detailText:
AI算力需求主导权已从训练侧全面转移至推理侧
2023年，算力需求几乎全部指向训练：模型参数越大、集群卡数越多，越可能在能力竞赛里领先，测算需求的方式就是数头部厂商要建多少个万卡集群。到2026年，同一套办法失灵了。一边是部分西部千卡级智算中心服务器上架率不足 50%、已上架设备实际利用率不足30%，年运营成本却超3000万元 [12] ；另一边是市场测算中国大模型日均Token消耗从2024年初的千亿级升至2026年6月的 500万亿级，两年多增长超过5000倍 [2] ，东部城市的低时延推理集群被描述为需要排队交付的「Token 工厂」 [3] 。同样叫算力需求，为什么一边闲置、一边紧张？差异不在总量，而 在需求 的形态：训练是一次性、集中、可以数清 楚的峰值，推理是分散、持续、随调用量不断复购的长尾。
AI 算力需求的主导权已经从训练侧转移到推理侧。训练需求按单次集群投入计量、随模型迭代脉冲式释放，推理需求按 Token 调用量计量、随应用渗透持续增长；继续沿用按训练集群规模估算需求的方法，会在区域布局、负载形态与容量规划三个方向同时产生错配。 把需求拆成峰值与长尾两类，是重新测算的前提。
两类需求不是同一条曲线上的前后两段，而是计量方式不同的两种量。 训练需求对应的是可以一次性算清的固定资产投入，推理需求对应的是随业务量滚动发生的运营成本。前者决定集群的规格与电力容量，后者决定节点的密度与利用率，用前者的尺子去量后者，是当下不少智算中心建成即闲置的测算根源。
2026 年被多个口径同时确认为需求结构的拐点。德勤《2026 科技、传媒和电信行业预测》给出的判断是，推理算力在整体 AI 计算中的占比达到 66%，首次超过训练[1]；IDC 与浪潮信息对中国 AI 服务器工作负载的测算是，推理占比由 2024 年的 65% 升至 2026 年的 70%、2028 年进一步升至 73%[2]；中国信通院《词元经济发展研究报告》给出的 2026 年推理算力占 AI 算力总负载比重为 70.5%[4]。三个口径的统计对象不同，但都指向同一个方向：推理负载已经超过训练负载。
支出端的变化更直接。2026 年全球 AI 推理算力支出预计约 233 亿美元，首次超过大模型训练支出约 190 亿美元[2]；推理硬件市场规模达到训练硬件的 2 至 3 倍，英伟达超过四成的收入已来自推理[2]。TrendForce 对北美五大云计算厂商的统计显示，2026 年 AI 推理算力增幅约 122%，增速是训练算力的两倍以上[7]。需求从「教模型」转向「用模型」，并不是模型能力不再重要，而是能力竞赛的投入从一次性的预训练，转移到后训练、测试时计算与规模化服务[9]。
把 2023 年与 2026 年放在一起，结构变化更清楚：2023 年 AI 推理负载仅占全部算力需求约三分之一，2026 年升至约三分之二[2]。中国信通院专家把这一变化概括为「训练上移、推理下沉」，即训练向少数大型集群集中，推理向城市与边缘下沉，研究机构给出的趋势判断是推理与训练的需求之比可能达到三比一[6]。对基础设施运营方而言，容量规划的对象随之改变：过去要回答「建几个万卡集群」，现在要回答「承接多少持续调用」。
训练需求的测算对象是单次任务，不是持续流量。经典测算框架把训练算力写作 C ≈ 6 × N × D，即每个参数、每个训练 Token 约需 6 次浮点运算[9]；据此，一次前沿训练需要的总算力由参数规模 N 与训练数据量 D 共同决定，落到采购端就是集群卡数乘以训练工期[9]。这与推理侧按调用量滚动计量的方式完全不同：训练任务立项时即可算出总量，训练结束，这笔算力消耗即沉入模型权重，不再产生后续调用[6]。
DeepSeek V3 是少数披露了完整训练参数的案例：6710 亿总参数的 MoE 架构、370 亿激活参数，在 2048 张 H800 上训练 55 天，披露的单次训练算力成本约 560 万美元[10]。这个数字需要按口径理解，它不含前期研发、消融实验与硬件总支出，同期披露的硬件投入超过 5 亿美元[10]。Epoch AI 的统计显示，前沿训练算力自 2010 年以来保持约 4.1 倍年增长、翻倍周期约五个月，训练成本约 2.4 倍年增长，单次前沿训练支出预计在 2027 年前后跨过 10 亿美元[9]；成本结构中硬件占 47%–67%、研发人员占 29%–49%、能源仅占 2%–6%[9]。
训练需求因此呈现两个可测算的特征。集中体现在客户结构上，有能力承担前沿训练投入的厂商与机构数量有限，单笔需求可以逐个列举；脉冲体现在时间分布上，需求随模型迭代周期成批释放，迭代间隙几乎没有新增负载。按训练需求规划容量，需要把「单次峰值」与「年度总量」分开——峰值决定集群规格与电力容量，迭代节奏决定全年平均利用率，两者不能用一个数代替。
训练需求增速见顶的原因不在投入不足，而在投入的边际产出下降。2026 年提出的一系列扩展规律研究指出，高质量文本的供给增速低于算力投入增速，重复与改写生成的派生 Token 价值递减，继续增加预训练算力买不到等比例的能力提升[9]。Epoch AI 估算全球高质量文本存量约 300 万亿 Token，按不同训练强度，可用数据的边界落在 2026 至 2032 年之间[9]。数据成为不可扩张的输入，参数与算力却仍可用资本扩张，两者之间的落差就是训练需求天花板的来源。

2023年，算力需求几乎全部指向训练：模型参数越大、集群卡数越多，越可能在能力竞赛里领先，测算需求的方式就是数头部厂商要建多少个万卡集群。到2026年，同一套办法失灵了。一边是部分西部千卡级智算中心服务器上架率不足 50%、已上架设备实际利用率不足30%，年运营成本却超3000万元 [12] ；另一边是市场测算中国大模型日均Token消耗从2024年初的千亿级升至2026年6月的 500万亿级，两年多增长超过5000倍 [2] ，东部城市的低时延推理集群被描述为需要排队交付的「Token 工厂」 [3] 。同样叫算力需求，为什么一边闲置、一边紧张？差异不在总量，而 在需求 的形态：训练是一次性、集中、可以数清 楚的峰值，推理是分散、持续、随调用量不断复购的长尾。
AI 算力需求的主导权已经从训练侧转移到推理侧。训练需求按单次集群投入计量、随模型迭代脉冲式释放，推理需求按 Token 调用量计量、随应用渗透持续增长；继续沿用按训练集群规模估算需求的方法，会在区域布局、负载形态与容量规划三个方向同时产生错配。 把需求拆成峰值与长尾两类，是重新测算的前提。
两类需求不是同一条曲线上的前后两段，而是计量方式不同的两种量。 训练需求对应的是可以一次性算清的固定资产投入，推理需求对应的是随业务量滚动发生的运营成本。前者决定集群的规格与电力容量，后者决定节点的密度与利用率，用前者的尺子去量后者，是当下不少智算中心建成即闲置的测算根源。

支出端的变化更直接。2026 年全球 AI 推理算力支出预计约 233 亿美元，首次超过大模型训练支出约 190 亿美元[2]；推理硬件市场规模达到训练硬件的 2 至 3 倍，英伟达超过四成的收入已来自推理[2]。TrendForce 对北美五大云计算厂商的统计显示，2026 年 AI 推理算力增幅约 122%，增速是训练算力的两倍以上[7]。需求从「教模型」转向「用模型」，并不是模型能力不再重要，而是能力竞赛的投入从一次性的预训练，转移到后训练、测试时计算与规模化服务[9]。

This article introduces Alibaba Cloud AIDBS, enabling AI agents to autonomously drive enterprise workflows with secure data access and seamless collaboration.
"Why did this metric drop recently? Break it down by region and category, and let's see how we should adjust next."
A conversation usually starts with a question and ends with an answer, but a piece of work has a much longer life cycle:
Models can already complete the analysis. What's missing is a mechanism to keep the work running. The enterprise AI Native approach that AIDBS represents reorganizes the work's context, data, permissions, and collaboration into a single task: the Agent keeps executing based on confirmed conclusions, while business judgment, authorization, and accountability stay with people. Where a task starts determines who is left carrying the work forward.
Much of the work inside an enterprise doesn't begin as a structured task. It begins as a group chat message: the background sits in earlier discussion, the materials are scattered across documents and message history, and the follow-up conversation loops back to DingTalk.
After reading the message, the Agent will confirm the metric definitions, query the data, break down the changes, determine the root cause, and form adjustment recommendations based on the existing rules.
But understanding correctly only solves the problem of "whether it knows." The next question is: is it allowed to use this data?
In a manual process, data permissions usually exist as a cycle of requesting, exporting, and handing off: a business user asks a question, the data team confirms the scope, and the result is handed back. Once the Agent starts using enterprise data directly, this kind of manual handoff can hardly carry all the control anymore.
Only after the data semantics and access boundaries are settled can the Agent complete the follow-up queries, dimension breakdown, and root-cause analysis, and generate an adjustment plan with evidence and items pending confirmation. The answer is ready, but the work is far from over.
But the automation here is not unlimited authorization. For confirmed recipients, information scope, and task actions, it can run automatically. The moment it touches a new budget, a change in resource priority, a new collaborator, or a new commitment to another team, the system stops and asks a human to confirm. Drawing the boundary of automation isn't just about whether the Agent can do it — it's about whether the accountability for that step can be transferred.

items.title: AI agents explained
items.detailText:
AI agents explained: A beginner-friendly guide to what AI agents are, how they work, their key types, benefits, and real-world use cases.
The distinction between AI agents and the bots or assistants you may already use is important. AI agents represent a shift from tools that respond to tools that execute on your behalf, while you stay in control of the outcome.
This guide breaks down what AI agents are, how they work under a user’s direction and oversight, and why they’re shaping the next wave of everyday AI use .
If you’re looking for an AI agent definition, here’s the simplest version: An AI agent is an artificial intelligence system designed to process goals, plan steps, and execute actions across tools on a user's behalf.
Unlike traditional chatbots that respond to one prompt at a time , AI agents can keep tasks moving across multiple steps without requiring input at each stage. Take a prompt like “clean up my inbox.” Given permission to read and act in your email, an agent can sort what is there, pull dates and deadlines onto your calendar, surface the messages most likely to matter, and draft replies for you to review before anything sends. One instruction, several steps, and you approve what goes out.
That approval step is the part to hold onto. Reviewing what an agent produces before anything is finalized helps keep the outcome in your hands.
But, how do AI agents really work? It comes down to a few key components.
AI agents are not limited to a single exchange. Many draw on two kinds of information: what you have said earlier in the conversation you are having, and details saved over time, like your preferences or past requests. So if you have already flagged that messages from your child’s school always matter, an agent can apply that the next time it sorts your inbox without being told again.
Once a goal is specified, an AI agent can break it down into smaller steps: sequencing tasks, comparing options against defined criteria, and selecting a next action without requiring input at each step. This capacity to process tasks in stages and select actions is what distinguishes AI agents from more rigid automation tools.
The AI agent systems that users are likely to interact with are typically composed of sub-agents, so that the AI agent system can work on different parts of a goal at the same time, or even different goals at the same time.
AI agents connect to external tools and systems through application programming interfaces (APIs), so their output is not limited to text. Through these connections, the system can update data, organize information, add a calendar item derived from an email, or trigger automation across different workflows.

items.title: 10 亿 Token 开源万只假鸟， AI 伪科普正在“污染”下⼀代的常识
items.detailText:
纷纷彩⽻戏群愚， 得来全不费⼯夫。  假作真时真亦假， 万鸟落枝⼀场空。
如果你是一名观鸟爱好者，也许会注意到这几天 App Store 上线了一款名为《鸣迹：观鸟手账》的新应用。
一个普通的记录类 App，安装包体积居然高达 1GB——而通常的科普图鉴类应用，大概是 100MB 左右的体量。
这个观鸟 App 既没有内置虚幻 5 引擎，也没有跑本地大模型，纯粹是因为开发者为了省下服务器资源，用一种做 3A 大作的思路，把海量的鸟类贴图全部硬塞进了本地包里。
但这也仅仅是形式上的敷衍，顺藤摸瓜找下去，你就会发现它真正的荒诞之处在于核心的数据来源——鸟类图鉴。
这款打着科普旗号的 App，其内置素材全部来自最近在开发者圈高调刷屏的一个开源项目——「全球鸟类贴纸库」。
与这个 App 同期上线的，还有一个支持 15 种语言检索的配套鸟类网站「Bird Album」。
不用去野外吹风淋雨，也不用懂半点鸟类解剖学，一台电脑、8 个窗口跑 AI 脚本， 不到一个星期，就能把全世界所有现生鸟类「一张不落」地全部画完，至于真不真实，根本不重要。
这位自称完全不会写代码的独立开发者，靠着 Vibe Coding 烧掉了超过 10 亿的 Token ，跑光了数次 200 美元顶配会员的周额度， 在不到一星期内， 就把全球 11,064 种现生鸟类 （后随名录更新调整为 11,011 种及 91 个亚种）做成了白边贴纸，然后向全网宣布「正式开源」。
随着这套贴图库堂而皇之地渗透进 App 和检索网站，知识上的次生灾害已经可见端倪。
一些本身并不具备专业辨识能力的自媒体和普通用户，正拿着这些连羽色、喙形等基本生物特征都存在严重错乱的 AI 贴图，煞有介事地拼凑着「专家级」的动植物科普图文与短视频，在社交平台上肆意传播，而作者对此还颇为得意。
纵使鸟类专家深表愤慨、其他独立开发者批评不断，他们却一概被作者归为「旧时代的残党、拒绝纺织机的工人」。
在这场由算力堆砌出来的幻梦里， 「垃圾进，垃圾出」的荒唐戏码 ，正借着 AI 的名义在一片机器人的赞誉声中高歌猛进。
首先是近乎「明抢」的抓取逻辑。AI 凭空画鸟极易胡编乱造，作者本身又没有专业数据库，怎么解决？
他去 iNaturalist 和维基共享资源里，把全球摄影师辛苦蹲守拍下的真实照片批量扒下来，拼成 3×3 的「九宫格」，直接喂给生图模型重绘。
根据作者自己的披露，在这 11,064 种鸟的参考照里，真正采用开放许可（CC0、CC BY 等）的仅有 1,986 种。剩下的绝大多数要么明确标注了「非商业使用」「禁止演绎」「保留所有权利」 ，要么甚至还有 2017 种连许可协议都没记 ，就被一股脑塞进了 AI 的熔炉。
等洗稿成 AI 贴纸后，作者反手就给它们打上自己的授权标签（最初甚至用了限制竞品使用的 PolyForm Shield 1.0 协议，后改为 CC BY 4.0），并轻飘飘地留下一句：如果某张贴纸参照了你的照片且你不希望被使用，请发邮件提 Issue，我们会在 7 天内撤下。
这种「先喂给 AI，苦主找上门再删」的强盗逻辑，在海外观鸟社区 Reddit 的 r/birds 版块直接引发了众怒： 「把别人的心血喂进抄袭机器，从来不是一件可以靠『事后申请退出（Opt-out）』就能洗白的事。」
为了在几天内强行凑齐一万多种鸟，还有另外一个雷霆的做法：冷门鸟找不到好照片，就拿几张残缺照片拼凑；模型画完后，交给另一个 AI 审核员打分。在测试中作者自己都发现，生图模型频繁造出令人啼笑皆非的怪物——
原本红色或蓝绿色的虹膜，被画成了死气沉沉的全黑眼珠；脚趾融成一团肉块；连蜂鸟这种极短腿的鸟，都被强行安上了一双麻雀式的大长腿。
要是重画两次还是画不对怎么办？作者定下的原则是：既不退回使用真实照片，也不留空， 而是「矬子里拔将军」，强行选个相对高分的图留下。
用纯工程学的暴力思维去搪塞严肃的科普问题，结果就是在初代开源仓库里，连项目自己设定的 AI 及格线（80 分）都没过的残次品高达 3,388 张（其中 109 张甚至低于 70 分），却依然被理直气壮地打包塞进了公开图库。
虽然后来作者在 11 月用另一套 AI 标准把这一万多张图重跑了一遍并宣布全部「过线」，但从头到尾，这套打着科普旗号的图库，都没有经过哪怕一位鸟类学专家的系统审校。
「有一回藤野先生将我叫到他的研究室里去，翻出我那讲义上的一个图来，是下臂的血管，指着，向我和蔼的说道：『你看，你将这条血管移了一点位置了。──自然，这样一移，的确比较的好看些，然而解剖图不是美术，实物是那么样的，我们没法改换它。现在我给你改好了，以后你要全照着黑板上那样的画。』」
这是鲁迅《藤野先生》中耳熟能详的片段。但令人错愕的是，时至今日，「美术大于事实」的观念在 AI 圈竟还有着如此广阔的市场。
在图库存在大量常识硬伤的情况下，作者依然热情推荐大家将这些贴纸拿去「做自然教育的课件、给孩子做鸟卡」，甚至提供了绑定 eBird、GBIF 等权威科研数据库编号的 CDN 接口；转头却又在说明文档里给自己叠了一层厚厚的免责甲：
「这些是插画，不是图鉴图版……发现画错了，欢迎提 Issue，鸟友的纠错是这个项目最需要的贡献」。
这也是整个开源项目最大的争议点：有没有能力核查一万多张图，是能力问题；但在产品上线、推向公众科普前是否做过专业把关，是态度问题。
作者所秉持的，是代码世界里最典型的「敏捷开发」思维——先上线跑通（Ship it），再靠社区提 Issue 纠错迭代。
作为开发者，似乎只要跑通了脚本、生成了图片、开源了代码，工作就算大功告成，至于知识是否准确，全盘甩锅给使用者和专业社区。把这种「先污染，后治理」的逻辑平移到自然科学领域，无疑是一场灾难。
以有「空中猛禽」之称的 游隼为例，如果只看贴纸图，外行人根本看不出问题，尤其是整个制图风格是写实画风，而不是动漫或者简笔画线条。
直到鸟友贴出对比图才发现，原本跗跖粗壮、爪趾强健有力的游隼，在 AI 笔下竟长出了一双孱弱细软的爪子。作者回查后才承认，原来脚本抓取的参考照片是从树下仰拍的，游隼的脚被腹羽和树枝遮挡。
当程序自动抠去树枝后，AI 直接「脑补」出了一副细爪，而负责把关的 AI 审核员对此毫无察觉。
结果 AI 画出来之后，鸟类最基础的折叠翼羽区（覆羽与飞羽的层级与结构关系）依然错得一塌糊涂。
「是插画不是图鉴」这种说法，并不能免责，原因不是「鸟类图鉴不能用画的」，传统手绘图鉴本来就不等于摄影照片。
但手绘取舍的底线，是每一笔都扎根于真实的物种解剖，并由懂行的人把关。优秀的博物画师会综合多只个体的长期观察，有意突出尾羽、喙形或换羽期的鉴别特征。

items.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.
The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.
Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:
Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.
Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.
Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.
Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks. You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases.
Dio Rettori discusses the operational realities of enterprise AI inference. Moving beyond fast token generation, he explores why inference requires dedicated systems engineering, tackles GPU utilization pitfalls, compares on-prem versus cloud TCO, and analyzes multi-agent latency determinism. He shares why teams must embed domain ontology directly into models rather than relying solely on RAG.
Henry Wilson shares actionable tools from the BBC Sounds re-architecture to help senior engineering leaders drive technical strategy. He discusses building buy-in, navigating active resistors, using RFCs and ADRs, and balancing tradeoffs - showing that effective software architecture is fundamentally about communication, relationship-building, and organizational influence.
The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI’s true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.
